Themes: Governance of the Federation and Netherlands Research Portal
A sustainable governance framework established for the Dutch federated research information ecosystem including parties maintaining Repository/CRIS systems, eDepot and OpenAIRE Graph.
SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance)
Repository/CRIS systems have adopted the updated metadata- and exchange-standards for high-quality research metadata that comply with international guidelines and meet national requirements.
WUR (tech lead), SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance, architect), KB (WISH)
Comprehensive full-text availability in Dutch repository/CRIS systems for enhancing primarily preservation, and secondary text-mining, AI-usage and Taverne-mechanisms.
WUR (tech lead), SURF (community management, legal advice, project assistance)
Comprehensive preservation achieved of Dutch scholarly output in the KB e-Depot.
Increase the visibility of Dutch research content in major international indexes.
Deliver a fully-functional, user-centered Netherlands Research Portal that serves as the primary discovery point for Dutch scholarly output.

legal structure for CC0 metadata and fultext copies:
1. CC0 metadata: For metadata to float freely between systems, we need to make sure that the legal framework of each piece of metadata (exactly specified metadata fields) is allowed to be used in analyses down the road; from publisher, through repositories and cris systems, to open scholarly knowledge graphs, to analysis in strategic reports. This requires that CC0 metdata is mentioned explicitly in the publishers negotionations. Publisher metdata is often the source of metdata. better to have it right at the source, than to repair afterwards.
